title: A ‘Distraction’ Reunion On ‘All Ball’, Just For You
summary: The NFL’s Thanksgiving weekend slate starts tonight, with the wholly manufactured “Thanksgiving Eve” game on Netflix. This slate features a ton of juicy matchups, almost as recompense for the previous two weeks of dreadful games that you and I have had to endure. Every one of the five-throwgasm showdowns spread out across the next six days(!) merits thorough analysis. Alas, because my All Ball co-host Arif Hasan was on the road all day yesterday, you the audience get David Roth instead. https://art19.com/shows/the-distraction/episodes/000e8d43-8c45-4d22-b035-1f0e5cbf58fe My old Distraction co-host is versed in football, so don’t be alarmed. You’ll still get plenty of chitchat about the games at hand. But Roth and I also carve out some time to marvel at the election results, to ask big-picture questions about the league’s desire to occupy every available time slot, and to discuss Portuguese egg tarts. Truly, a feast for the ears. As always, we do NOT talk about gambling or fantasy football. Roth tried to get in a brief fantasy note, but I quickly shut that talk down and had my friend summarily killed after we’d recorded this episode. Didn’t want to do it; felt I owed it to him.

title: Aaron Rodgers Nukes Mike McCarthy, Then His Own Career
summary: To provide further detail on the Pittsburgh Steelers' late-night benching of Aaron Rodgers, the quarterback himself appeared on Wednesday's edition of The Pat McAfee Show . Essentially, Rodgers said that he would never play for the team again, and he described head coach Mike McCarthy as inattentive, sleepy, and "unhealthy." In response to this TV appearance, the team has waived Rodgers . The Steelers' benching of Rodgers came after his dismal performance in Sunday's 19-16 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles, and there's some logic behind it for purely football reasons. But the way the news was delivered was the strange part: Tuesday at 11 p.m. ET, through a team spokesperson. At the time, it wasn't even clear if Rodgers himself knew he was being benched for the team's game this Friday against Denver.

title: Hark! Royal Gossip Approaches!
summary: Have you ever wondered what a pack of specially trained bloodhounds might do for your personality? Ever considered the societal benefits of locking up your enemies in the Tower of London? Would a special dispensation from the Pope smooth things out for your most fraught marriage prospects? Could you deal with being hot enough to change the course of humanity? Prepare yourselves for the majesty of Royal Gossip ! Rachelle Hampton and the Normal Gossip team are back with a new miniseries that dares to ask the question: What is history if not gossip? Over the course of four episodes, we’ll explore the most sordid tales from one of the most charmed and chaotic periods in English history: The Wars of the Roses. Oh, and did we mention we’ll have royalty? In each episode of Royal Gossip , Rachelle will be joined by our dowager queen Kelsey McKinney!

title: ‘Paper Tiger’ Is A Thrilling Homecoming For James Gray
summary: Americans are forever returning to their origins, because we are always beginning again. At the start of the 20th century, three-fourths of my ancestors were still in Europe; my mother’s parents did not come over until the end of the second World War. To think of all the accidents and contingencies that brought me here, to this laptop in this café writing about the latest film by James Gray, is enough to trigger vertigo in anyone. Where does my story start? With my birth, or when my parents met on an airplane, or when my dad’s grandparents met as new immigrants in Queens? Is it only beginning now, as I type these words? Has it even begun yet? I think Gray might understand. A director of New York City crime sagas and classically toned period pieces, his films probe the intimate in search of the mythic, and frequently achieve a kind of outer-borough biblicality. Paper Tiger , his latest and quite possibly his best, is a story of shifting loyalties inside a Queens family called the Pearls. Irwin (Miles Teller) is an engineer, a “facts and figures” guy with a moderately successful small business, a house in Fresh Meadows, and a sea of expenses rising all around him. His wife Hester (Scarlett Johansson) wants to move to suburban Great Neck; his sons need tuition for private school and the Ivy League stamp that Irwin believes will vault them out of the ethnic middle class, and allow them to achieve what their Pratt-educated father never could. Over Labor Day weekend of 1986, the Pearls are visited by Irwin’s brother, Gary (Adam Driver), a recently divorced ex-cop with shiny suits, a sports car, and seemingly liquid cash flow. Swooping into their two-story brick home with a steak meal hand-delivered from Peter Luger, he wants to cut Irwin in on a lucrative opportunity, joining their security and engineering knowledge to consult on the clean-up of the outlandishly polluted Gowanus Canal. New York is changing, the Italian mob is in decline, and the canal’s new landowners are all Russian Jews like the Pearls, though of more recent vintage. “Communism’s over,” Gary explains. “Everyone wants their piece of the pie.”

title: San José State President Enlisted Harry Edwards To Sabotage Students’ Pro-Palestine Encampment
summary: As heartening as it was to see the wave of student-led Gaza solidarity encampments across college campuses in the spring of 2024, it was just as appalling to see the crackdowns from those same schools' administrations. Across the world, university leaders showed that they were willing to sacrifice the safety of their own students and faculty, rather than divest from any companies that had financial ties to a state committing active genocide. The most closely covered protest was at Columbia University, where the school ultimately sent in the NYPD to dismantle the camp and assault students. The response dragged on for months; a WhatsApp group strategized on how to get the protestors deported, and put together a list of targets. Columbia graduate Mahmoud Khalil is currently appealing a deportation order, after he was held in ICE detention without criminal charges for over 100 days. On the other side of the country in 2024, UCLA's security and local police stood by as masked goons attacked students within the Gaza solidarity encampment, and tossed fireworks at them. Roughly 30 of the students and faculty attacked have sued UCLA for civil rights violations. Because of reporting last week from Bradford William Davis and Kaya Henkes-Power at the publication Eyeblack , another school administration's grimy efforts have come to light, two years later. When San José State University students put together their Gaza solidarity encampment in 2024, they convened at the Victory Salute statue, a monument on campus honoring the school's alumni Tommie Smith and John Carlos for their raised fists at the 1968 Summer Olympics. The statue was created in 2005 by the Portuguese artist Ricardo Gouveia, who goes by the moniker Rigo 23.

title: This Thanksgiving, I Hope Someone Gets You Cookies
summary: Drew Magary’s Thursday Afternoon NFL Dick Joke Jamboroo runs every Thursday at Defector during the NFL season (except when there's a game on a Wednesday). Got something you wanna contribute? Email the Roo . You can also read Drew over at SFGATE , and buy Drew’s books while you’re at it . It’s the holiday season in Chicago, and I am six years old. My grandma Neenie is staying at her apartment in the Streeterville neighborhood of the city, just south of the John Hancock building. Neenie and Grandpa spend the bulk of the time living down in Palm Beach, Fla., but they’ve kept the Chicago apartment because this is where they raised my mother and her three siblings, and because my family lives there now, in an apartment farther uptown. I love it when Neenie and Grandpa visit, because I know that Neenie will take me to Water Tower Place and buy me shit. Water Tower Place is located just a few blocks away from my grandparents’ apartment, on the tony stretch of Michigan Avenue and right next to the old Chicago Avenue Pumping Station, after which the mall is named. You enter Water Tower Place from the ground floor, and then ride up into the mall alongside a series of little waterfalls cascading down between the twin escalators. I’m a grade-schooler, so I’m already predisposed to loving a good escalator ride. The fact that this one has waterfalls makes it, in my innocent mind, the most magical escalator in the world. Like riding up to heaven, if heaven had a McDonald’s in it.
